items.what: A trainer row's required level (types/Forever.lua:83-89 declares GetTrainerServiceInfo's 4th return `number?`) is replaced with 1 when missing, and the row is persisted in TweaksForeverCharDB.trainer.
items.why: Model.Choose computes `ready = spell.level <= level`, so an `unavailable` row saved with level 1 is drawn as trainable now (SPELLBOOK_TRAINABLE text, backplate and glow in Paint, sorted first by InOrder) and returned by TweaksForever.API as available, with nothing logged; the wrong value outlives the session in the saved variable. Does Forever ever return a nil level for a KEEP row, and if so should the row be skipped (as rows with no lineID are) rather than saved as level 1?
items.reason: The fallback is real and silent (`level = level or 1` is saved to TweaksForeverCharDB.trainer and Model.Choose then marks the row ready), but whether it ever fires, and whether a missing level means 'no level requirement' (in which case 1 is the right value), is a client fact: the repository only declares the 4th return `number?`. The `or 1` also narrows `number?` to TFTrainerSpell's `level number`, so it cannot simply be deleted, and skipping the row instead would change behaviour. Settle it in game: at a class trainer, dump GetTrainerServiceInfo(i) for each `unavailable` row and see whether the 4th return is ever nil and what the trainer window shows as its level requirement.

Can a verifier find any reader of ns.WhatsNew or WhatsNew.Message outside this file? If not, the live-roots line in the project skill should drop it too.

Make Message a file-local function and drop the export, its type field in types/Namespace.lua and its Live roots entry, or keep the Model-per-file convention and add a spec that calls it?

items.quote: - Explain campsite benefits. Hovering a camp feature (a Camp Tent, Mana Well, Anvil and the rest) shows what sitting nearby gives you, such as "Stamina increased for 1 Hr", and whether you have it now, with the time left. A benefit you have carries your buff's own numbers ("Stamina increased by 8"); the game sets them when you gain it, so one you don't have shows none. Hovering a campfire lists every benefit a camp can give: the ones you have in green with their time left, the rest in grey. Your Campfire Nearby buff adds the benefits you have and which way the campfire is, once you have lit it or sat by it; your Camp Benefits buff adds the ones you haven't gained yet.

items.quote:
BagSize = function(c)
		return c.size
	end,
	BagItems = function(c)
		local i = 0
		return function()
			i = i + 1
			if i <= c.size then
				return i, c.Items[i]
			end
		end
	end,
items.what: tests/bagslayout_spec.lua:145-156 re-implements ns.BagSize and ns.BagItems, whose canonical home is Core/Core.lua:47-62, instead of loading Core as tests/core_spec.lua does; the layout pass under test (Bags/Sections.lua:79, Bags/Reagents.lua:173,191-192) therefore runs against the spec's copy of the slot iterator, not production's.
items.why: The BagItems stub is a line-for-line copy of the production iterator (index counter, `index <= size`, `container.Items[index]`), not a recorder stub like Feature/Init. Differences: production BagSize is `container.size or C_Container.GetContainerNumSlots(container:GetID())`, the copy only `c.size`; production BagItems reads `container.size or 0` once, the copy rereads `c.size` each step and errors on nil. Both look like accidental simplification. If the rule for which buttons hold a slot changes in Core (its comment says it mirrors EnumerateValidItems and avoids GetBagSize caching), this spec keeps passing on the old rule. Question for the verifier: can the spec load Core/Core.lua for these two helpers (core_spec shows the env it needs: Settings, C_AddOns, CreateFrame, geterrorhandler) without Core's own Feature/Init/Active displacing the stubs the spec relies on, or is the copy the deliberate standalone-stub convention and so a fixture?
items.reason: The lens's Do not flag covers test fixtures: this spec stubs the whole ns (Feature, Init, Active, OnSettingChanged, Gear) and BagSize/BagItems are part of that injected seam, the same ground on which ledger item 6e5eaf1600 was dismissed. For the owner: the swap is feasible, a scratch probe that loads Core/Core.lua into a private ns and borrows its two helpers passes, but that is a fixture redesign, not a defect.

items.why: Both model the same frame API surface; differences are deliberate (bagslayout has height drift, parent tracking and 5-point unpack; runtime asserts not-in-combat and keeps a point list, fires OnShow/OnHide). A GetPoint/SetPoint fix would need two edits, but a shared helper would break the standalone-spec rule, and other specs (reagents, sections, gear_ui) are outside this slice.
items.reason: Bag Region keeps multiple points and layout/scale state, while the Frames fake drives scripts, combat/load order and movable-window geometry. The matching method names are the client frame interface; their data/state semantics differ. Sharing a general frame framework would couple standalone tests without consolidating an addon algorithm.

Sections/Reagents are exercised against that seam, while core_spec tests the real iterator. The settled standalone ns preambles and thin headless tests do not require importing Core's unrelated client initialization.

items.quote: assert(fits or bag:GetScale() == 0.75, "fits on screen: " .. bag:GetHeight() .. " x " .. bag:GetScale())
items.what: The bag-fit assertion does not enforce the promised minimum scale; an unreadably small fitting bag passes
items.why: Sections.Fit must clamp at the native 0.75 minimum. This assertion only checks fit OR equality at 0.75, so fitting at 0.1 passes. The fixture initially lacks an anchor and cannot exercise rescaling; supplying a native anchor makes both original production and a temporary want=0.1 mutation pass, as do sections/reagents model specs. Preserve existing fit checks and add an actual shrink case with lower-bound assertion.
items.reason: tests/bagslayout_spec.lua:323 asserts `fits or bag:GetScale() == 0.75`, which a bag shrunk to 0.1 also passes, so the promised 0.75 minimum scale is not enforced. Add a fixture that can shrink and assert scale >= 0.75? A new assertion is not a behaviour-preserving edit.
